name: Car wash (express tunnel)
summary: Ground-up express exterior tunnel wash (80–160 ft tunnel, ~2,400–5,500 SF building) on 1–1.5 acres with 15–30 free vacuum stalls. The budget splits into building + site work (baseline here) and a separately purchased tunnel equipment package (conveyor, arches, dryers, chemical, controls, pay stations) plus vacuum system, which together add $1.0–2.5M. Evidence is moderate: one full franchisor line-item table (Tommy's Express 2020 FDD, 2020 $), a secondary report of the 2026 Tommy's FDD, one consultant development budget, and one Texas registration.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Building SF: MMCG example 4,307 SF (w3); Texas registration 4,586 SF (w4); EB3 80-ft conveyor example 2,400 SF (w5). Mid 4,300 SF ≈ 120–130 ft tunnel with equipment room.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Sites need 'roughly 1–1.5 acres' (w5); MMCG example 'just over one acre' (w3) → 0.67–1.0 sites per acre.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Vacuum stalls (which double as customer parking): 15–30 per site (w5); 29 in MMCG example (w3).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Building + site work per site, EXCLUDING tunnel equipment and vacuums (line items). Evidence years mixed: Tommy's 2020 FDD site work & construction $1.70–2.64M + building package $1.01–1.07M = $2.70–3.70M (2020 $, glass flagship building, w1); Tommy's 2026 World Model site-specific $288k + building construction $961k + structure $283k + components $227k ≈ $1.76M (2025–26 $, compact model, w2); MMCG West Coast example hard cost incl. site work $3.2M (2025, w3); EB3 example ~$2M construction incl. site work for 2,400 SF / 80 ft (w5); Texas registration $1.5M for 4,586 SF (2025, likely building-only, w4). Mid $2.75M = midpoint of the 2025-dollar cluster ($1.76M compact – $3.2M West Coast) nudged up toward the Tommy's 2020 range, which would be higher after escalation (build script escalates evidence, not this mid). Low = compact/World-model; high = flagship 130-ft glass tunnel on a difficult site.

perSF.method: perPrimaryUnit ÷ sfPerPrimaryUnit (2.75M / 4,300 ≈ $640). MMCG reports ~$740/SF of building for hard cost incl. site in a West Coast market (w3). Site work inflates $/SF.

scope.notes: Building (tunnel + equipment room + office), MEP, slabs/trench drains, reclaim pits, and on-site work (stacking lanes, vacuum canopy footings, paving, utilities, landscaping). Excludes tunnel equipment package and vacuum system (lineItems), signage (ffe), land, soft costs, water/sewer tap and impact fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (Tommy's World / compact, 1.6/2.75 ≈ 0.58→0.65); premium/luxury ≈ glass-tunnel flagship and Flex-model ranges (w2 Flex building+site ≈ $5.7–7.3M is outside 'luxury' and treated as an outlier).

systemSplit.method: From Tommy's Express 2020 FDD Item 7 trade breakdown (w1), average of low/high columns, building+site only ($3.20M). Mapping: GC general requirements→01; concrete→03; masonry→04; building structure (steel/glass package)→05; exterior finishes + ½ building components→07; windows/doors + ½ components→08; flooring + interior finishes→09; signage→10; mechanical (HVAC & plumbing) split ½/½ to 22/23, snowmelt→23; electrical + lighting→26; site work split 40/35/25 to 31/32/33; misc & landscaping→32. Div 05 is high because Tommy's uses a proprietary steel-and-glass building; masonry/CMU tunnels shift share from 05 to 04.

lineItems.name: Tunnel equipment package (conveyor, arches/brushes, dryers, chemical, backroom, controls, pay stations/POS)

cost.method: Tommy's 2020: equipment $871,299–$928,371 + wash controls $118,950–$156,660 + POS $76,534–$92,876 = $1.07–1.18M (2020 $, w1); MMCG 2025 equipment & systems $1,651,000 incl. 29 vacuum stations (w3) → ≈$1.3–1.4M ex-vacuums; 2025 trade estimates $1.4–2.1M typical (w5). Mid $1.3M; years mixed (2020 evidence noted).

lineItems.notes: Usually bought from the equipment manufacturer/distributor, not the GC. Includes water reclaim in Tommy's package.

lineItems.name: Free-vacuum system (central turbine, arches/booms, piping) for 15–30 stalls

cost.method: Tommy's 2020 vacuums $103,160–$272,078 (w1); Tommy's 2026 World vacuum system $87,400–$147,462 and Flex $364,096–$469,910 (w2). Mid ≈ $175k for ~22 stalls.

lineItems.notes: Vacuum canopies/arches are often bundled; stall paving is in baseline site work.

lineItems.name: Water reclamation system
lineItems.notes: Add only if the equipment package excludes reclaim (Tommy's package includes it). Often required by permit.

lineItems.name: Tunnel exit / apron snowmelt
lineItems.notes: Cold climates only; already reflected in the high end of the baseline.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Signage + office furniture: Tommy's signage $101,448–$102,688 (2020, w1) and $95,000–$102,005 (World, 2026, w2); furniture & fixtures $2,500–$17,000 (w1). Range widened for independents with simpler pylon signs.

pctOfHard.method: Tommy's 2020 soft costs $137,000–$620,500 incl. water tap fee $15,000–$250,000 (excluded by definition) → $122k–$370k on $2.7–3.7M building+site ≈ 4.5–10% (w1); Tommy's 2026 World soft $122,347–$272,169 on ≈$1.76M ≈ 7–15% (w2); MMCG ~$430k excl. contingency on $3.2M hard ≈ 13% (w3). Mid 10% (of baseline hard; equipment line items carry little soft cost).

softCosts.notes: Type-specific: water/sewer tap fees can be large ($15k–$250k in w1) — excluded here as impact/tap fees. Franchise fee $50,000 (Tommy's). Traffic/stacking studies often required.

hard.method: MMCG example carries contingency of 10% of hard costs (w3); mid 8% with separate design contingency.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard (baseline + equipment + vacuums) $2.6–7.0M × 1.06–1.15 soft, excl. land. Consistent with irecruit/MMCG industry range '$3.85 million to well over $10 million' including land (w3, w5) and Tommy's 2026 totals $3.48M–$8.52M including fees and working capital (w2).
